evidence_rows.source: Mathieu Lewin, Coulomb and Riesz gases: The known and the unknown, arXiv:2202.09240v2, Sec. VI, PDF pp. 58-59, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09240
evidence_rows.quote: phase transition is that R_s,beta,mu is not reduced to one point
evidence_rows.verdict: Primary review describes phase transition as nonuniqueness of Gibbs point processes. It explicitly says its finite-beta R_s,beta,mu is defined for s>d; it does not supply a general finite-beta DLR construction in the long-range 3D case.

evidence_rows.source: Lewin, arXiv:2202.09240v2, Sec. VI.B, PDF p. 65, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09240
evidence_rows.quote: it is believed to form a solid
evidence_rows.verdict: For d=3, s>3, review reports numerical BCC/FCC phase diagram; for s<3, analogous long-range diagram is described as a belief. These are expectations, not a proved theorem or a single quantified conjecture.

evidence_rows.source: Lewin, arXiv:2202.09240v2, Sec. IV.B, Conjecture 38, PDF p. 43, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09240
evidence_rows.verdict: Conjecture 38 is at zero temperature; it must not be substituted for P0309.

candidate_formalization: For some s>3, density rho>0 and finite beta>0, show a grand-canonical infinite-volume Gibbs state at chemical potential mu with nontrivial periodic order and corresponding symmetry-related nonunique Gibbs states. The exact meaning of periodic order, quantifier over s, beta threshold, and ensemble is not specified by the intake and must be fixed before a solution claim.
